Let’s talk about something that really matters—Chapter 5: Building Lifelong Antiracist Habits and Considering Legacy.
Here’s the thing: antiracism isn’t a one-and-done achievement. It’s not something you can simply check off your to-do list and move on from. Instead, it’s a lifelong practice—a way of showing up in the world that takes ongoing care, curiosity, and a willingness to keep learning and growing.
So, what does it actually mean to build antiracist habits? It’s all about weaving reflection, accountability, and action into the fabric of your daily life. That might sound like a lot, but really, it starts with being open to new ideas, ready to listen, and willing to be challenged—even when it’s uncomfortable.
And let’s be real: there’s no finish line here. There will always be more to learn, more to unlearn, and more to do. The work isn’t ever truly done.
One really important piece at this stage is thinking about legacy. Every choice you make right now shapes the world future generations will inherit. Becoming a “good ancestor” means acting with an eye toward the long-term impact of your actions. It’s about asking yourself, “Am I contributing to a more just and equitable world for those who come after me?”
Now, let’s get practical. What does building lifelong habits actually look like? It’s about continuous learning—diving into books, podcasts, and conversations that broaden your perspective on race and justice. It’s about community involvement—joining groups, organizations, or movements that are pushing for real change. It’s about mentoring and supporting others—sharing what you’ve learned, offering resources, and encouraging folks who are newer on this journey. And it’s about reflecting on your legacy—asking yourself, “What kind of world do I want to help create? What will I be remembered for?”
This stage is all about keeping up your momentum and not slipping into complacency. Remember, antiracism is a collective effort—when individuals take action together, even the smallest steps can add up to powerful, lasting change.
The journey we’ve explored so far isn’t easy—but it is so necessary. It calls for honesty, courage, and compassion, both for yourself and for others. When you commit to this ongoing work, you help dismantle the systems that keep injustice in place, and you play a part in building a world where everyone gets the chance to thrive.
